properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 21 at 7:49AM MST until October 21 at 8:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
TORFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 815 AM MST.

* At 749 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Prescott Valley, moving northeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Prescott Valley, Prescott, Chino Valley, Dewey-Humboldt, Downtown
Prescott, Oak Knoll Village, Whipple, Embry-Riddle Aeronautical
University, Prescott Regional Airport, Prescott Rodeo Grounds,
Yavapai County Fairgrounds, Mingus Mountain, Fain Lake, Willow
Creek Reservoir, Watson Lake and Lynx Lake.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 69 between mile markers 283 and 296. State Route 89
between mile markers 311 and 320. State Route 89A between mile
markers 318 and 339.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Potato Patch Campground, Playground Group Campground, Lynx
Campground, Eagle Ridge Group Campground, Hilltop Campground, Acker
Park, AC Williams Granite Creek Park, Watson Lake Park and
Mountainview Park.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

CMAMtext: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 8:15 AM MST. Take shelter now. Check media.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 8:15 AM MST. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 21 at 10:11AM AST until October 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Exposed northwesterly and north-facing beaches of
Puerto Rico, Culebra, and the northern US Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 21 at 9:34AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end of this
week. There is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage
next week after northeasterly winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 21 at 5:53AM MST until October 22 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An upper-level trough will bring a deep surge of subtropical and
tropical moisture into our region. Showers and thunderstorms will
develop across much of northern and central Arizona early
Wednesday morning and continue through Thursday evening. Stronger
thunderstorms will bring threats of Flash Flooding, while more
prolonged rainfall could lead to elevated flow in streams,
rivers, and washes.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 21 at 6:45AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
Patchy dense fog continues in the Kansas and Nebraska border area.
McCook and Oberlin have recently reported visibility as low as a
quarter of a mile. The fog will continue for another few hours
before burning off between 10 and 11 AM CDT.

Wildlife, stalled vehicles and other road obstructions will be
difficult to spot. Low visibility may cause the time to slow down
and stop to be longer than the time you are able to see ahead.
